original_value: Service-oriented systems increasingly depend on dynamic discovery, recommendation, and composition of distributed web services, yet varying quality of service metrics can degrade overall user satisfaction. This article examines how deep learning and nature-inspired optimization can be combined to support QoS-aware service recommendation and adaptive composition in volatile environments. The proposed framework integrates collaborative filtering signals with attention-based feature extraction and evolutionary search to rank candidate services, estimate composite QoS, and mitigate sparsity and cold-start issues. Experimental discussion highlights hybrid modeling, scalability considerations, and practical challenges in selecting component services under changing workload conditions.

This article explores how deep learning and nature-inspired optimization may be combined to enable QoS-aware service recommendation and adaptive composition in volatile environments. The proposed framework blends collaborative filtering signals with attention-based feature extraction and evolutionary search to rank candidate services, estimate composite QoS, and address sparsity and cold-start problems. The experimental discussion emphasizes hybrid modeling, scalability concerns, and the practical difficulty of choosing component services under shifting workload conditions.
